simple.meaning: חָתַם (châtham) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to close up; especially to seal.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 27 times across Leviticus, Deuteronomy, 1 Kings, Nehemiah, Esther, and 6 more, beginning at Leviticus 15:3. Its contexts include family line, kingship, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָתַם (H2856).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: חָתַם (châtham) / H2856 is traced through Leviticus 15:3, Deuteronomy 32:34, 1 Kings 21:8, Nehemiah 10:1 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: to close up; especially to seal
definitions.usage: make an end, mark, seal (up), stop.
